prompt: Can you tell me the workspace role of whoever reacted with 🎉 (tada) to the message about deploying the redesigned onboarding flow to production, posted in a channel where Carlos Vega is also a member?
binding_note: Route: WORKSPACE_MEMBERSHIP(user_teams) -> USER -> REACTION -> MESSAGE -> CONVERSATION -> CONVERSATION_MEMBERSHIP. The target workspace membership belongs to whichever user's own reaction (tada) sits on the onboarding-deployment message, and that message's channel must separately have a conversation_membership record for Carlos Vega. All three conditions (reactor identity, emoji, message content+channel, and that channel's membership by Carlos Vega) must bind to the same message/channel; a tada reaction on a different message, or a tada reaction on the right message but in a channel Carlos Vega does not belong to, does not qualify.

obligations.name: onboarding_reactor_membership
obligations.description: Identify the workspace membership (user_teams row) of the user whose own 'tada' reaction is on the message announcing the onboarding-flow production deployment, where that message's channel also has a conversation_membership for Carlos Vega; report that membership's role. No user satisfies every condition simultaneously.
obligations.scope: ordinary workspace-wide lookup across channels the acting user can see

task_spec.text: Find who reacted with tada to the onboarding-deployment announcement in a channel where Carlos Vega is also a member, and report that person's workspace role.

access_plan: Search channel histories/search.messages for text mentioning the onboarding flow deployment to locate the anchor message and its channel (#frontend). Use reactions.get on that message to enumerate reactors and emoji names, isolating any 'tada' reactions. Use conversations.members on the message's channel to check whether Carlos Vega (real_name lookup via users.list/users.info) is a member there. Separately, search other channels' histories for 'tada' reactions to confirm whether any such reaction lands on a message in a channel where Carlos Vega is a member. Cross-referencing shows no user's tada reaction satisfies both the message-content and channel-membership conditions together, so the workspace-membership lookup returns no match.
